_what: The threshold overfetch margin ε (D-074): a similarity threshold τ maps to a squared-L2 bound l2² ≤ 2(1-τ) on unit vectors; the candidate phase holds only the PQ approximation of l2², so it keeps rows with PQ_dist ≤ 2(1-τ) + ε and rerank applies exact τ. ε is a MEASURED high quantile (p999) of |adc - true l2²| — the quantile IS the recall contract (a qualifying row is missed only if its own PQ error exceeds ε, at most 1-in-1000).

real-v1.queries: the 60 real corpus queries x all rows (n=180000 pairs)
real-v1.note: ε = p999 rounded up (~7% headroom). The 0.1% of pairs above ε (up to max 0.352) are the accepted miss budget — that IS the p999 contract. tests/rederive_epsilon.rs re-measures and asserts p999 <= ε.

hash-v1.queries: stride sample of stored vectors x all rows (n=180000 pairs)
hash-v1.note: Retained as the paired data series (NOT shipped). tests/pq_margin.rs still measures it. On the hash corpus the shipped ε=0.30 bounds this trivially.

delta.mechanism: The hash embedder produces a handful of near-identical motif vectors, so PQ reconstruction is near-exact and |adc - true l2²| ≈ 1e-6 — a degenerate artifact. Real 768d all-mpnet embeddings are CONTINUOUS and spread across the sphere, so product quantization (96 subquantizers, 256 codes each) leaves a real reconstruction error whose p999 is ~0.28 in squared-L2 units. The margin the recall contract actually needs is ~300000x what the hash corpus implied. This validates the D-074 margin-injection paths against natural geometry: at ε=0.30 the relaxed bound genuinely overfetches and rerank genuinely prunes back, where at 1e-6 both were vacuous.

cost._what: The price of ε=0.30 is OVERFETCH: the relaxed candidate bound l2² ≤ 2(1−τ)+ε admits rows the exact τ then rejects. Measured on real-v1 (60 queries × 3000 rows, scan-all nprobe=64) by tests/rederive_epsilon.rs::epsilon_overfetch_cost_on_real_v1. overfetch_ratio = candidates admitted / rows clearing exact τ; admit_pct = fraction of the whole corpus the candidate phase kept.
cost.finding: Overfetch is MATERIAL: median 2.7–6.3x (peaking ~6.3x at moderate selectivity τ≈0.40), worst-case up to 50x on tight answers. At BROAD selectivity (τ=0.20) the candidate phase admits 98.2% of the corpus — the answer set is already most of the corpus, so the overfetch RATIO is modest (2.7x) but the ABSOLUTE work is a near-full scan. This is exactly where the S9 state-budget refusal is the safety valve: at production scale a broad-τ query admits admit_pct·N rows and is REFUSED past THRESHOLD_STATE_BUDGET (100k) rather than reranked without bound — verified firing at an injected budget of 200 on real-v1.
cost.state_budget_refusal: Scale-dependent. On real-v1 (3000 rows) the production 100k budget never fires; the refusal was demonstrated with an injected budget=200 at τ=0.1 (named, cites D-074). At N rows a broad-τ query admits ~admit_pct·N candidates; the refusal fires when that exceeds THRESHOLD_STATE_BUDGET.
cost.improvement_path: Filed as issue #8 (do NOT tighten ε below the receipted p999 — the quantile IS the recall contract). Two candidate mechanisms: (1) asymmetric bound tightening — the +ε margin only needs to cover the p999 of the ONE-SIDED error adc − true_l2² > 0 (rows the approximation over-estimates are already safe), so a tighter one-sided quantile could halve the admitted set without touching recall; (2) a residual/refinement pass — a cheap second-stage exact distance on the admitted candidates before full rerank, bounding the rerank input at moderate selectivities where overfetch peaks (~6x at τ≈0.40).

_honest_wall: This is the real number the README's recall/threshold economics stand on, not the hash corpus's flattering 1e-6. ε is the MOST geometry-sensitive constant in the ledger: it MUST be re-derived per real-embedding corpus and per generation (C-3/C-6), forever.
